samples.summary: `deleteSelectedImageInline` deletes 1 char at the stored image offset without re-validating the block/image, so a stale image selection either throws or deletes the wrong character
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2242-2252 does `const { blockId, offset } = selectedImage; docStore.snapshot(); doc.deleteText({ blockId, offset }, 1);` with no `doc.findBlock(blockId)` / `findImageAtOffset` check. Its sibling `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2256-2267) deliberately uses `findBlock` and re-checks `findImageAtOffset`, with a comment naming the exact hazard: "a block a remote peer just deleted". `MemDocStore.deleteText` -> `findBlockInAnyArray` throws `Block not found: <id>` (memory.ts:214-217, 331-353), so on that same remote-deletion scenario the Delete/Backspace route (`imageKeyHandler`, editor.ts:2309-2313) throws out of the keydown listener instead of returning null. If the block still exists but offsets shifted (remote insert before the image, or the text-selection cut path described in the next finding), the delete silently removes an unrelated character — data loss with an undo snapshot taken around it. This delta's new cut tests are the first coverage of the `imageDeleteHandler` wiring; the cut path happens to be guarded by the provider, the Delete path is not.

samples.summary: When a text selection and a click-selected image coexist, the text branch of `handleCut` deletes the text but never clears the parent's image selection, leaving `selectedImage` pointing at a shifted offset
samples.evidence: The new test at copy-integrity.test.ts:285-303 institutionalises the state where `selectedImage` and a text range are live at once (`selectImageAt` then `_setSelectionForTest`, asserting `getSelectedImage()` is still non-null after the copy). The cut counterpart is unguarded: `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1233-1253) takes the `hasSelection()` branch, calls `deleteSelection()`, and never touches `imageSelectionProvider`/`imageDeleteHandler`, so `selectedImage.offset` in editor.ts is left pointing into text that has moved. The render path (editor.ts:1853-1855) will then draw resize handles around whatever image now sits at that key, and a following Delete goes through the unvalidated `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2242). The same stale state is produced by the copy branch, but only cut mutates the document.

samples.summary: `resetAfterDocumentReplace` clears the caret, selection and layout cache but not `selectedImage`, leaving an image selection that references a block id from the previous document
samples.evidence: editor.ts:3745-3757 resets `pending`, `cursor`, `selection` and `layoutCache`, but `selectedImage` is only nulled in `dispose` (editor.ts:3762) and in the mouse/key handlers. After a document replace with an image selected, `imageKeyHandler` (editor.ts:2281-2282) still reports the selection as live and absorbs Delete/Backspace into `deleteSelectedImageInline`, which calls `doc.deleteText` on a blockId that no longer exists — `MemDocStore.findBlockInAnyArray` throws `Block not found` (memory.ts:353). Even without the throw, keystrokes are swallowed by a selection the user cannot see.

samples.summary: `getSelectedImage` / `selectImageAt` / `updateSelectedImage` call the throwing `doc.getBlock`, so their `if (!block) return` guards are dead and a stale block id throws instead of returning null
samples.evidence: `Document.getBlock` throws `Block not found: ${blockId}` (document.ts:174-188) — it never returns a falsy value, so `const block = doc.getBlock(...); if (!block) return null;` at editor.ts:3654-3655 (and 3640-3641, 3667-3668) can never take its early-return. The author knew this: `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2256-2262) explicitly uses `findBlock` "not `getBlock`: the latter throws" for exactly the stale-block case. The new tests call `getSelectedImage()` after a cut (copy-integrity.test.ts:343); if the block had been removed rather than just the inline, the call would throw instead of yielding null.

samples.summary: The image copy/cut fix depends on the browser firing a native `copy`/`cut` on an always-empty hidden textarea with a collapsed selection; the new tests dispatch those events synthetically, so that dependency is unverified
samples.evidence: `imageKeyHandler` consumes Cmd/Ctrl+C and Cmd/Ctrl+X and returns true *without* `preventDefault` (editor.ts:2295-2300) on the assumption the native clipboard event follows. The textarea is kept empty (`this.textarea.value = ''` at text-editor.ts:669, 746, 758, 763, 794) and the image path is precisely the case where there is no text selection, so in engines that suppress copy/cut for a collapsed/empty selection the key is swallowed and nothing reaches the clipboard — worse than before, since the key is now consumed. The same assumption breaks the `EditorAPI.copy()/cut()` entry points (editor.ts:3333-3343), which drive `document.execCommand('copy'|'cut')` and are documented to fail on an empty selection: a toolbar/context-menu Cut over a selected image would be a no-op while Cmd+X works. copy-integrity.test.ts:334/351 dispatch the `cut` event by hand, so nothing here is exercised end-to-end.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. editor.ts:2242-2252 `deleteSelectedImageInline` destructures the stored `selectedImage` and immediately calls `doc.deleteText({ blockId, offset }, 1)` with no `findBlock`/`findImageAtOffset` re-validation, unlike its sibling `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2256-2267) which guards both and whose comment names the exact hazard ("a block a remote peer just deleted"). The throw path is real: document.ts:277-279 -> memory.ts:214-217 -> findBlockInAnyArray -> `throw new Error('Block not found: ...')` at memory.ts:353. It is reachable from the Delete/Backspace branch at editor.ts:2309-2313, dispatched from the live keydown listener at text-editor.ts:854 (registered text-editor.ts:560) — and critically, TextEditor's own stale-block guard for "deleted by a remote collaborator" sits at text-editor.ts:858-870, i.e. AFTER the imageKeyHandler dispatch, so the image route bypasses it. I enumerated every `selectedImage` write in editor.ts (1239, 2247, 2304, 2324, 2342, 2508, 2518, 3644, 3649, 3762): none is driven by an external/remote document change, and render()/getSelectedImageRectCommitted (1853-1855, 2362-2368) only fail to find a rect without clearing the selection, so staleness persists. Concurrent remote edits are a real scenario in this product (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts, peer cursors editor.ts:1197/1590). Outcome is an uncaught throw out of the keydown listener, or — when the block survives but offsets shifted — silent deletion of an unrelated character wrapped in an undo snapshot. Squarely in the correctness lane (missing guard / crash / data loss) and blocking.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: handleCut's text branch (text-editor.ts:1233-1253) calls saveSnapshot/deleteSelection without ever consulting imageSelectionProvider or imageDeleteHandler — those are only reached inside the `!hasSelection()` branch (1224-1232). Nothing in editor.ts clears `selectedImage` on document mutation or text-selection change (all clears are at 2247, 2304, 2324, 2342, 2518, 3649, 3762 — image delete, Escape, arrows, catch-all key, click-elsewhere mousedown, explicit API, dispose), so after a text cut `selectedImage` keeps a now-shifted {blockId, offset}. Consequences are real: the render path (editor.ts:1853-1855) keys rects by `${blockId}:${offset}` and will draw handles around whatever image now sits there, and a subsequent Delete goes through imageKeyHandler (2281-2282) into deleteSelectedImageInline (2242-2252), which does `doc.deleteText({blockId, offset}, 1)` guarded only by `readOnly || !selectedImage` with no findImageAtOffset validation — deleting an arbitrary character. The coexisting state is not test-only: handleImageMouseDown returns early for BUTTON/INPUT/menu targets (2453-2464) without clearing selectedImage, while clearSearchMatches(true) (3393-3402), the undo selection restore (2025-2038) and restoreLocalCursor (3737) all set a text range without clearing it. The new test at copy-integrity.test.ts:285-303 exists exactly to lock in that both are live at once. No refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The omission is real — resetAfterDocumentReplace (editor.ts:3745-3757) clears pending/cursor/selection/layoutCache but not selectedImage, and no other code in the reset path clears it. However the harm path the finding describes is unreachable, so it is not blocking under the correctness rubric. `selectedImage` is a per-initialize closure variable (editor.ts:1239) set only by user-driven handlers (mousedown at editor.ts:2508, key handler, and the selectImageAt API at editor.ts:3644). A repo-wide grep (excluding node_modules) shows exactly one production caller of resetAfterDocumentReplace: docs-view.tsx:360; all other hits are packages/docs/test/view/pending-style-editor.test.ts. That call sits in the same mount effect that constructs the editor (initialize at docs-view.tsx:327, store.setDocument at 356, reset at 360) — synchronous, before any pointer/key event can run, and onEditorReady at line 341 is just a React setState (docs-detail.tsx:217). Therefore selectedImage is provably null whenever the reset runs, and the described chain (imageKeyHandler editor.ts:2281-2282 absorbing Delete into deleteSelectedImageInline editor.ts:2242-2252 with a dead blockId) cannot fire. Other document-replace writers bypass this API entirely: apply-imported-content.ts:224 writes through a detached YorkieDocStore at import time, and the live remote path (docs-view.tsx:378-394) uses refresh/restoreLocalCursor/validateCursorPosition. That makes this a defensive gap in an unreachable branch — minor, not a blocking defect.
